sources.entry: TetherShot - Capture pixel-perfect iPhone screenshots from the macOS menu bar over USB or Wi-Fi.

summary.one_liner: TetherShot is a native macOS menu-bar and window app that captures screenshots from a tethered iPhone (USB or Wi-Fi) or an Android phone (via ADB) and saves them to a folder and the clipboard.
summary.what_it_does: TetherShot shows connected iPhones and authorized Android phones in a Mac app window and captures their screen with one click or a global hotkey (⌘⇧7). USB iPhone capture uses native AVFoundation, while Wi-Fi capture runs pymobiledevice3 over a RemoteXPC tunnel kept alive by a root LaunchDaemon (tunneld). Android capture uses ADB discovery and the device's native screencap PNG. Each PNG is saved to a chosen folder (default ~/Pictures/TetherShot) with timestamped filenames, optionally in per-device subfolders, and can be copied to the clipboard. Options include hiding devices, a preferred hotkey device, optional paste-after-capture (needs Accessibility access), Dock and menu-bar visibility, launch at login, and in-app self-update from signed GitHub releases. It is distributed via Homebrew cask, a signed DMG, or an npm CLI that builds from source.
use_cases: capture iPhone screenshots to a Mac folder over USB
wireless iPhone screenshots without a cable
grab Android phone screen from a Mac via ADB
save phone screenshots for documentation or app store mockups
quick screenshot hotkey for connected phones
copy phone screenshot straight to clipboard
how_to_run: git clone the repository, cd TetherShot, ./build.sh
notable: USB iPhone capture via native AVFoundation with no extra setup beyond Trust This Computer
Cable-free iPhone capture over Wi-Fi through Apple's developer-services tunnel, even when the phone is locked
Android capture of the native framebuffer over USB or wireless debugging
In-app updater verifies the GitHub release digest and Developer ID signature before replacing the app
Local-first: no account, no analytics, no servers
caveats: Built and tested only on macOS 26 (Tahoe) with iOS 26; requires macOS 14+
Wi-Fi capture needs pymobiledevice3 installed and a root LaunchDaemon set up once with an admin password
First USB capture triggers a macOS Camera permission prompt because the screen is delivered via the AVFoundation camera bucket
